steps.text: Stir shrimp, tomatoes, onion, cilantro, lime juice, salt, pepper, and garlic together in a large glass bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until the flavors combine, at least 1 hour. Serve cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp Salsa
raw_recipe.description: Shrimp, tomatoes, red onion, cilantro, and lime juice combine for a unique and refreshing chunky salsa perfect for scooping up with tortilla chips.
raw_recipe.name: Shrimp Salsa

recipeInstructions.text: Stir shrimp, tomatoes, onion, cilantro, lime juice, salt, pepper, and garlic together in a large glass bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until the flavors combine, at least 1 hour. Serve cold.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous! Refreshing and a little different from the norm. Doubled the recipe and added a few jalepenos. I let it sit over night and the flavors were great. Wonderful recipe, will make again and again!

I saw several people looking for salad shrimp. What they are referring to is the canned shrimp that are very small. Instead, I used 1/2 pound of large frozen shrimp, cooked in the microwave until pink, about 1 minute, 30 seconds. I then cut the shrimp into bit sized pieces after cooling, cleaning and peeling. I also added 2 large stalks of celery and an avocado. Top it off with 1/4 cup sweet chili sauce for some extra zing. This disappeared in my house!

I found the original recipe bland. I added (adjusted for your liking)
 ½ jalapeño diced 
 1 table spoon EVOO 
 1 table spoon red wine vinegar
 1 table spoon white vinegar
 ½ teaspoon cayenne pepper
 ½ teaspoon cumin seed/cumin
I also would use larger shrimp next time. I might even cook and season them myself and then chill them before hand. Although with some minor additions a good simple light recipe.

This is the best. I make it all the time. I double the recipe, use larger cooked shrimp cut in half after removing tails. Replace tomatoes with small can of rotel original tomatoes w green chilis (after discarding some of the juice), adds a little heat. And I don't add the lime juice until rite before serving because I think it cooks the shrimp more and makes them a little tough. Excellent recipe. My guests always request it.

this was a great addition to our party. i grilled regular size shrimp, the red onion and some jalepanos. although i see now that that is not even on the recipe...oops....i doubled the recipe so it took a lot longer for me to make. had a lot of compliments, light and tasty. i served with bite size torilla chips. i can't wait to make this again with my fresh tomatoes from my garden. thanks for the post WW!

Very mild and bland. I am from Colorado, where things spice up a bit. I added Tapatio hot sauce the first time. Not hot, just more flavor. The second time, I used a homemade salsa, drained so it was not watery, fresh lime juice (1 lime), a diced avocado. Yumm! Much better. 

Made for a nice light dinner with tortilla chips.

It was excellent , can't wait to make it again. However I had to make tomato modifications becuz i couldn't find ripe tomatoes around New Years, so I substituted fresh store bought salsa and a can of no sodium petit diced tomatoes and drained them. I also used fresh sauted shrimp. 
Yum can't wait to make it again in the summer months.

I made this twice in the past week and it was gone in the blink of an eye. The only thing I did differently was to add one very large chopped jalapeno - other than that, this is perfect as is. I will definitely be making this on a regular basis. Also definitely let sit overnight so the flavors develop. Oh, I used Tostito's Scoops - I found the other scoops too hard.

This was a hit! Everyone loves it and it is all we have been eating for the past 2 days! I followed the recipe exactly. The only extras I added were 1 diced Jalapeno (1/2 with seeds and 1/2 without) and 1 diced avocado. Will be making this over and over again! So fresh and light!

This is an awesome fresh salsa. For those who love fish tacos you will love this. I did add 1/2 seeded jalapeno for spice and 3 garlic cloves as we love garlic. When I make this the next time I plan to use raw shrimp, cook, then dice. I am not a big fan of salad shrimp as it does not have as much flavor as regular shrimp.

This was sooooo good! I had some small, already cooked shrimp that I wanted to use up in an appetizer, and made this. Yummmm!
Followed the recipe exactly, with one addition: as others have suggested, I minced up a little bit of jalapeño and tossed it in. That added just the right amount of heat. 
The fresh cilantro made this so tasty. Warning, though, 15% of the population taste soap when the eat cilantro, so my husband wouldn't even try it. But it is my favourite herb, so bring it on!

This is a flavorful, low-calorie recipe, especially for those watching their waist lines. I put it on lettuce and skip the tortilla chips. I make this a couple times every summer for lunch and dinner.
So quick and easy and everyone loves it. Be sure and double the recipe because it goes very quickly!

I got a kick out of the reviewers who couldn't find "shrimp salad" !!! Really good summer meal choice. Only modification was to add some chopped jalapenos . I will make this again as my garden's Romas are starting to ripen!!!
This is a delicious, easy recipe! I also could not find salad shrimp so I bought medium shrimp and cut them in half! I doubled the recipe because it was for a party and it was gone in 10 minutes!
Recipe is great. I added sweet Chile peppers and chopped avocado for additional flavor. My family loved it.

Oh my this is sooooooo good! I’ve made 3 batches in the last 2 weeks and it disappears quickly. I added a little fresh jalapeño and an diced avocado for even more goodness. Such a low calorie and healthy treat! I’ve turned at least 4 others onto this recipe already too - it’s too good not to share!

Brought this to a Barbecue, but they weren’t going to cook hamburgers or hotdogs. So I stepped it up and came up with this as an appetizer. There wasn’t ANY LEFT! The only thing I changed was one of your reviewers mentioned using Picco de Gallo instead of cutting everything up. Saved me a lot of time and thank goodness I doubled the recipe. The only problem now is my family will expect me to bring from now on!

This is for Justine and those that couldn't find shrimp salad.....it's "salad shrimp", the little tiny ones that you can get in Belair (and other stores) butcher dept. or in cans located with the tuna, etc.
Great recipe, too bad shrimp is not cheaper!
